advances: A planar auxiliary scalar stress obstruction. No common individual cap budget, critical menu, or same-source contact identities are assumed.

proof:
For the normalized affine denominator, set $c(\epsilon)=\exp[-M_\lambda^{-1}\int_{K_\lambda}\log(x+\epsilon)\,dm]$. The function $\log(\epsilon c(\epsilon))$ is strictly increasing because its derivative is $1/\epsilon-\mathbb E[1/(x+\epsilon)]>0$ for the normalized volume law. It tends to $0$ at infinity because the ratio $(x+\epsilon)/\epsilon$ converges uniformly to one. It tends to $-\infty$ at zero because the volume logarithm converges to a finite value. This follows from $\int_0^1(2x+2\lambda)|\log x|\,dx<\infty$. It therefore takes the value $-\beta/\lambda$ at a unique $\epsilon_\lambda$. As $\lambda\downarrow0$, this equality forces $\epsilon_\lambda\to0$, since the normalized log at each fixed positive $\epsilon$ stays bounded. For large indices the $x$ marginal is $(2x+2\lambda)/(1+2\lambda)$. With $\epsilon_\lambda<1$, the absolute logarithm is dominated by $|\log x|+\log 2$ for $x>0$. Dominated convergence gives the normalized limit $\int_0^1 2x\log x\,dx=-1/2$, so $c_\lambda\to\exp(1/2)$ and $\lambda\log(1/\epsilon_\lambda)\to\beta$. In particular $\epsilon_\lambda/\lambda\to0$.

The left facet has length $2\lambda$, constant positive logarithm $\beta/\lambda$, outward normal $-e$ and rate $\beta$. It shrinks to the origin, giving the stated atom. The top and bottom edges are parametrized by $x$ with bounded Jacobians and have uniformly vanishing logarithmic integrals near $x=0$, by the integrable bound just proved. The right facet stays away from zero. This identifies the entire surface defect.

The gradient-length weighted inverse measure is $dm/(x+\epsilon_\lambda)$. At positive rate $s$ the coordinate is $x=c_\lambda^{-1}e^{-s/\lambda}-\epsilon_\lambda$ and $|dx|/(x+\epsilon_\lambda)=ds/\lambda$. The rate density is $2(x+\lambda)/\lambda$ on $0<s<\beta$ for all small $\lambda$. On any compact positive-rate subinterval it tends to $2$ and the spatial points converge to zero. The total inverse mass is
$$
2+2(\lambda-\epsilon_\lambda)\log((1+\epsilon_\lambda)/\epsilon_\lambda)\longrightarrow 2+2\beta .
$$
Off the origin the inverse measure tends to $dm|_{K_0}/x$ at rate zero by dominated convergence on sets bounded away from $x=0$. Its mass is $2$. The positive-rate defect on $(0,\beta)$ already accounts for the remaining $2\beta$, leaving no additional endpoint defect. This proves the uniform-rate formula including the open and closed tail conventions.

At every point of $K_\lambda$ the load of the threshold caps is the length of $\{s\in[0,\beta]:s\ge r_\lambda\}$, since all parameter values capture a point with $L_\lambda\ge1$. The empty cap contributes nothing. The parameter values at supporting cuts have $ds$-measure zero, so the same formula holds for the actual boundary allocations. Thus $W_\lambda=\beta-r_\lambda$ and the physical signed measure vanishes. All caps have continuous normal a positive multiple of $e$. Keep $s$ as an original cap-law mark. For fixed $0<s<\beta$ the section of $H_{\lambda,s}$ is at $x=c_\lambda^{-1}e^{-s/\lambda}-\epsilon_\lambda$, has coarea $2(x+\lambda)$ for normal $e$, and has logarithm $s/\lambda$. Its log defect is $2s\delta_{(0,s)}$. The corresponding inverse selection is the actual restriction to rates at most $s$, giving limiting defect $2\delta_0\otimes\operatorname{Leb}|_{(0,s)}$, and the cap-selected exterior defect is zero. Integrating over the original law gives the asserted inverse capture density $2(\beta-R)\delta_0$. Equivalently, multiply the full inverse measure before taking limits by the continuous function $\beta-r_\lambda$ of the recorded rate. This latter proof directly gives the result if the threshold labels are forgotten and all their limiting record locations coincide. At each $0<R<\beta$, the inverse reserve satisfies $R(2\delta_0)+\int_R^\beta 2\delta_0\,ds=\beta(2\delta_0)$, with the same equality using the left value at $\beta$.

Finally averaging the exact load proves $\beta_\lambda=\beta-\lambda A_\lambda$. Dominated convergence with the same integrable bound gives $A_\lambda\to\int_0^{e^{-1/2}}-2x\log(\exp(1/2)x)\,dx=1/(2\exp(1))$. The stated identity with the averaged budget follows exactly. For fixed $s>0$ the threshold cap mass tends to the entire limiting area, while the empty cap always has mass zero. Thus the example uses a continuous threshold law with no common individual critical volume, and the scalar remainder is the displayed bounded remainder of size $O(\lambda)$.

statement:
For every $0<\beta<1$ and sufficiently small $\lambda>0$, let $K_\lambda=\{(x,y):0\le x\le1,\ |y|\le x+\lambda\}$, $M_\lambda=1+2\lambda$. There is a unique $\epsilon_\lambda>0$ for which $L_\lambda=c_\lambda(x+\epsilon_\lambda)$ has volume-mean logarithm zero and minimum $e^{-\beta/\lambda}$. Put $r_\lambda=\lambda(-\log L_\lambda)_+$ and $e=(1,0)$. The full positive-log surface defect with rate retained is $2\beta\delta_{(-e,0,\beta)}$, and the gradient-length weighted inverse-volume defect is
$$
N_e=2\delta_0\otimes \operatorname{Leb}|_{(0,\beta)}
$$
with no rate-zero defect. Thus $N_e$ is the uniform-rate kernel image of the surface defect with the normal forgotten.

Use the actual cap law assigning weight $ds$ to $H_{\lambda,s}=\{L_\lambda\ge e^{-s/\lambda}\}$ for $s\in[0,\beta]$ and weight $1-\beta$ to $\{x\ge2\}$. Its boundary load $W_\lambda$ satisfies $W_\lambda-\beta+r_\lambda=0$ identically up to cap-law-null allocation choices. The physical signed measure and its Jordan marginals are zero, so every finite convex physical stress and perspective-entropy test on that measure has equality. The canonical full inverse density at rate $0<R<\beta$ is $2\delta_0$, its cap-law-selected density is $2(\beta-R)\delta_0$, and the part captured by normals other than positive multiples of $e$ is zero. For the open tail at $R\ge\beta$ the density is zero, with left density $2\delta_0$ at $\beta$. For the exact averaged normalized cap volume $\beta_\lambda=M_\lambda^{-1}\int_{K_\lambda}W_\lambda\,dm$, one has $\beta_\lambda=\beta-\lambda A_\lambda$ with $A_\lambda=M_\lambda^{-1}\int_{K_\lambda}(-\log L_\lambda)_+\,dm\to1/(2\exp(1))$, and $W_\lambda-\beta_\lambda+r_\lambda-\lambda A_\lambda=0$.

Consequently scalar stress, its convex and entropy tests, the actual cap selection law, the exact averaged volume budget and the full uniform inverse-rate kernel do not imply a strictly positive universal noninside captured share. These caps are allowed to have different individual volumes.
